correctness.rationale: For Q_d, d>=2, adjacency Hamiltonian J A with J nonzero, two positive local irreversible sink rates, the dark space is the orthogonal complement of the two-source cyclic subspace B=span{H^j|a>,H^j|b>}; any nondecaying eigenvector of H-iK/2 must lie in ker K and thus be dark. Finite-dimensional evolution on B decays, even with Jordan blocks. Uniform mixed initial state yields eta=dim(B)/2^d independently of rates. Distinct Walsh eigenspaces indexed by l have rank 1 at l=0,d. If separation k=d, parity of intersection with b is constant across each l-subset, giving rank 1 in all d+1 levels. For 1<=k<d, both parity signs occur among each 1<=l<=d-1 (connectivity of Johnson l-subset graph and availability of an inside-outside exchange), giving rank 2, hence total rank 2d. Checks of exact Walsh parity rank for every 2<=d<=11 agree. The proof is all-dimensional; finite tests only corroborate.
